tools.description: Ask the user a question and wait for their response. Use this when you need clarification, want to validate assumptions, or need the user to make a decision. Each question has 2-4 options; the user can also provide custom text.
tools.name: ask_user

header.description: Short label (max 12 chars) displayed as a tag, e.g. "Auth method", "Library".

multiSelect.description: If true, the user can select multiple options. Default: false.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means.

label.description: Display text for this option (1-5 words).

markdown.description: Optional preview content shown when this option is focused.

question.description: The question to ask the user. Should be clear and end with a question mark.

tools.description:
Also supports org-mode block syntax: `#+BEGIN_BASH` + command + `#+END_BASH`

I execute native shell commands. Returns exit code, stdout, stderr. For file operations, I prefer dedicated tools (read, edit, write, glob, grep). Shell is reserved for system commands — git, npm, docker, compilation, testing, process management, etc. Default shell is platform/config dependent (Windows usually Git Bash; Unix usually bash/sh); the optional shell parameter can select another native shell for one-shot commands.

**Do NOT use bash for programming logic.** Data processing, JSON manipulation, text analysis, computation — use the `script` tool (native Node.js) instead. Do NOT invoke python, node -e, perl, or awk via bash for these tasks.

**Persistent sessions** — pass `session` to keep a shell process alive across calls:
- State persists: CWD, environment variables, shell functions, aliases
- If the session is busy, your command text is written to stdin (useful for interactive prompts)
- Set `timeout` to a small value (e.g. 1000) to start a long-running process and return immediately — then call `bash_output({ session: "name" })` to check on it later
- Use `bash_list` to see all active sessions, `bash_kill` to terminate one
tools.name: bash

command.description: The shell command to execute using the selected native shell syntax.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to cwd. In persistent session mode, cwd only applies when creating a new session; use cd or a new session name for existing sessions.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does.

run_in_background.description: Deprecated. Use session with small timeout instead.

session.description: Persistent shell session name (e.g. "dev", "git"). When set, the shell process stays alive between calls — CWD, env vars, and shell state persist. If the session is busy (running a previous command), input is written to stdin. Omit for one-shot execution (default).

shell.description: Override the native shell for this command (one-shot only, not for persistent sessions). On Windows, commands must use the selected shell syntax. Default: git-bash. Use git_bash_no_pathconv for Git Bash with MSYS path conversion disabled (sets MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*); this is useful for ssh/scp/docker/kubectl/remote commands where POSIX paths like /tmp must not be rewritten to Windows paths.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 120000 (2 minutes). For session mode, set to a small value (e.g. 1000) to start a long-running command and return immediately without waiting.

tools.description: Terminate a persistent shell session and its process tree. The session is removed and cannot be reused (a new session with the same name can be created).
tools.name: bash_kill

tools.description: List all active shell sessions with their status, PID, uptime, working directory, and last/current command.
tools.name: bash_list

tools.description: Check the status and output of a persistent shell session. ONLY for sessions created via bash with the session parameter — one-shot bash returns output directly and does NOT need this tool. By default returns only the last command's output (clean, focused). Use tail=N to see the full session history buffer instead.
tools.name: bash_output

tail.description: Show last N lines from the full session buffer (overrides default "last command only" behavior). Use for history/scrollback.

wait.description: Wait up to N milliseconds for new output before returning (default: 0). Useful for polling a running command until it produces output or finishes.

tools.description: Navigate back in browser history (like clicking the back button).
tools.name: browser_back

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Click an element on the page using its ref from browser_snapshot. Example: browser_click({ ref: "e2" }) clicks the button with [ref=e2].
tools.name: browser_click

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Close the browser connection. Frees resources. Use when done browsing.
tools.name: browser_close

tools.description: Close a specific browser tab. If no tab is specified, closes the active tab.
tools.name: browser_close_tab

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description:
Execute JavaScript in the browser page context and return the result. Use for extracting data, checking DOM state, or performing actions not covered by other tools. The expression is evaluated in the page's global scope.

Examples:
  document.title
  document.querySelectorAll("a").length
  JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll("h2")].map(e => e.textContent))
tools.name: browser_eval

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Fetch a URL using the browser's real session — inherits cookies, auth tokens, and login state. Requires the Chrome Extension (stealth mode). Use for accessing authenticated APIs or pages that require login. Returns status code and response body.
tools.name: browser_fetch

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Clear a text field and type new content. Use for form inputs, search boxes, etc. The field is first selected and cleared, then the new value is inserted at once.
tools.name: browser_fill

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

value.description: Text to fill in. Use empty string to clear the field.

tools.description: Navigate forward in browser history.
tools.name: browser_forward

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Open a new browser tab and navigate to the given URL. The new tab becomes the active tab.
tools.name: browser_new_tab

url.description: URL to open in the new tab.

tools.description:
Open a web page in the browser. On first call, connects to (or launches) the browser via CDP. Subsequent calls navigate to the new URL. Returns page title and URL after load.

Connection priority:
1. If `cdpUrl` is provided, connects to that WebSocket URL directly
2. If LUX_CDP_PORT env is set (Android), connects to that port
3. Discovers already-running Chrome with CDP on well-known ports
4. Auto-launches Chrome/Chromium (if installed) with CDP enabled

Tab behavior: By default navigates the active tab. Pass `tab` to target a specific tab. Use browser_new_tab to explicitly open a new tab.
tools.name: browser_open

cdpPort.description: CDP port to discover targets via HTTP (e.g. 9222).

headless.description: Launch Chrome in headless mode (no visible window). Default: false.

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

url.description: URL to navigate to (e.g. "https://example.com"). Protocol is auto-added if missing.

tools.description: Press a keyboard key. Use for Enter to submit, Tab to move focus, Escape to close modals, ArrowDown/ArrowUp for dropdown navigation, etc.
tools.name: browser_press

key.description: Key name: "Enter", "Tab", "Escape", "Backspace", "Delete", "ArrowUp", "ArrowDown", "ArrowLeft", "ArrowRight", "Space", "Home", "End", "PageUp", "PageDown", or any single character.

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. Returns the image as an attachment. Use to visually verify page state, check layouts, or see rendered content.
tools.name: browser_screenshot

fullPage.description: Capture the full scrollable page instead of just the viewport. Default: false.

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Scroll the page or a specific element. Use to reveal content below the fold, navigate long lists, or scroll a specific container.
tools.name: browser_scroll

ref.description: Optional element ref to scroll within (for scrollable containers).

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description:
Get an accessibility snapshot of the current page. Returns interactive elements with refs (e.g. [ref=e1]) for use with browser_click, browser_fill, etc., followed by the page content as clean Markdown (extracted via Readability). Always run this after navigation or when you need to understand the page structure.

Example output:
  - heading "Example Domain" [level=1]
  - textbox "Search" [ref=e1]
  - button "Submit" [ref=e2]

  --- Page Content ---
  # Example Domain
  This domain is for use in illustrative examples...
tools.name: browser_snapshot

interactive.description: Only show interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs). Default: false.

maxContentLength.description: Maximum characters for the page content Markdown section. Default: 10000. Increase for long articles, decrease for quick interactions.

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: List all open browser tabs with their IDs, URLs, and titles. The active tab is marked with →. Use tab IDs with other browser tools.
tools.name: browser_tabs

tools.description: Type text character by character into a focused element. Unlike browser_fill, this triggers keyboard events for each character — useful for autocomplete, search suggestions, and live-validation fields.
tools.name: browser_type

delay.description: Delay between keystrokes in ms. Default: 50.

tab.description: Target tab. Number = exact tab ID. String = fuzzy URL/title match. Omit = active tab.

tools.description: Cancel a scheduled cron task. Provide either the task id (from cron_schedule result) or the tag you assigned. Cancelling by tag removes ALL tasks with that tag.
tools.name: cron_cancel

id.description: The id of the task to cancel (returned by cron_schedule).

tag.description: Cancel all tasks with this tag.

tools.description: List all your scheduled cron tasks (created by this session).
tools.name: cron_list

tools.description:
Schedule a delayed or repeating message. Fires by sending a message to the target session (like a timed link_post). Omit target to message yourself. Use target="*" to broadcast to all sessions.

Use cases:
- Remind yourself to check on something later
- Periodically monitor a service or task
- Send a scheduled message to another session

Duration format: "30m", "1h", "2h30m", "1d", "1d6h" (d=days, h=hours, m=minutes, s=seconds).
tools.name: cron_schedule

message.description: Message to send when the timer fires. Should clearly describe what to do.

repeat.description: Optional. Repeat interval after first fire. Same format as delay. Omit for one-shot.

tag.description: Optional. Human-readable tag for easy cancellation later.

target.description: Optional. Target session name. Omit = send to self. Use "*" to broadcast to all sessions.

tools.description: Manually trigger context curation to compress the canvas. Use when the canvas is getting long, context feels cluttered, or you need to free token space for intensive work ahead. The curator will intelligently fold old or irrelevant blocks while preserving important context. You can optionally provide a hint about what topics are currently important so the curator knows what to keep. Returns a summary of what was preserved and folded.
tools.name: curate

hint.description: Optional curation hint — what topics, conversations, or information are currently most important and should be preserved. E.g. "We are debugging a C++ memory leak in the mover module — keep everything related to mover, destructors, and glibc". This helps the curator make smarter decisions about what to keep vs fold.

reason.description: Brief reason for manually triggering curation (e.g. "canvas is too long", "preparing for complex task").

tools.description: Show the currently active persona with its tool permissions, loaded skills, and any overlay modifications.
tools.name: current_persona

tools.description: I modify a file by finding an exact string and replacing it. The target string must appear exactly once (unless replace_all is set). I always read before editing. To create entirely new files, I use write. For large changes (>200 lines), I split into multiple sequential edit calls — each targeting a small, precise region — to avoid output truncation by the provider.
tools.name: edit

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to edit.

old_string.description: The exact string to find and replace. Must be unique in the file unless replace_all is true.

replace_all.description: If true, replace ALL occurrences of old_string instead of requiring exactly one match. Defaults to false.

tools.description: I fetch a URL and return its content as Markdown. For HTML pages, I extract the main content using Mozilla Readability and convert it to clean Markdown. For non-HTML content (JSON, plain text, XML), I return it directly. Useful for reading web pages, documentation, API responses, etc.
tools.name: fetch_markdown

max_length.description: Maximum characters to return. Defaults to 20000. Increase for long documents, decrease for quick lookups.

raw.description: If true, return raw content without HTML-to-Markdown conversion. Useful for JSON APIs or when you need the original format. Default: false.

timeout.description: Request timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds).

url.description: The URL to fetch (http or https).

tools.description: Search for personas by keyword, matching against name, display name, and description.
tools.name: find_personas

keyword.description: Keyword to search for in persona names and descriptions.

tools.description: Get the current date and time. Use this when you need to know what time it is — for example, to gauge how long you've been working, or to timestamp a decision.
tools.name: get_current_time

tools.description: I find files by name pattern. Supports *, **, ? wildcards. Returns up to 500 matches. To search file contents rather than names, I use grep.
tools.name: glob

path.description: Base directory to search in. Defaults to cwd.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files (e.g. "*.ts", "**/*.ts", "src/*.js"). Basename-only patterns like "*.ts" match recursively under the base directory.

tools.description: Expand a subgraph centered on a node. Returns the center node, edges, and neighbor nodes within N hops.
tools.name: graph

tools.description: I search file contents by regex pattern. Supports output modes (matching lines/file paths/counts), context lines, case sensitivity, multiline, file type filtering. To find files by name pattern, I use glob.
tools.name: grep

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Only for content mode.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Only for content mode.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Only for content mode.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output. Defaults to true for content mode.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}"). Basename-only patterns match recursively under the search path.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N entries. 0 = unlimited (default).

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines. Default: false.

offset.description: Skip first N entries before applying head_limit. Defaults to 0.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines with context, "files_with_matches" shows only file paths (default), "count" shows match counts per file.

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to cwd.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents. Uses ripgrep/JavaScript-style regex: use `a|b` for alternation, not grep basic-regex `a\|b`.

regex_dialect.description: Regex dialect. "ripgrep" uses ripgrep/JavaScript-style regex. "grep-basic" converts common grep basic-regex escapes (\|, \(, \), \+, \?, and numeric intervals like \{1,3\}) before searching. "auto" first tries ripgrep, then retries safe grep-basic alternation compatibility when no matches are found.

type.description: File type to search (e.g. "js", "py", "ts", "rust", "go", "java"). More efficient than glob for standard file types.

tools.description: Retrieve full details of any knowledge entry by its short id (n_/e_/t_). For nodes: shows props, related edges, anchored notes. For edges: shows src/dst node summaries. For notes: shows full content + anchor info. Automatically updates access stats and refreshes <memory> hints.
tools.name: inspect

id.description: Short id: n_xxxx, e_xxxx, or t_xxxx

tools.description: Cancel an async link_wait subscription by its id. Use this to disarm a previously registered trigger.
tools.name: link_cancel_wait

id.description: The subscription id returned by link_wait(async=true).

tools.description: List all active Lux sessions with their id, name, and status. Use this first to find which sessions are available before using other link tools. Returns session id (for programmatic use) and name (human-readable label set in WebUI).
tools.name: link_discover

scope.description: Discovery scope. "local" (default) returns only this instance's sessions. "cluster" also includes remote public sessions from connected instances (requires Hub).

tools.description: View the current state of another Lux session. Returns what the user sees in WebUI: status, tasks, tool calls, and text output. Use scope to control detail level. Use turn= to paginate through conversation history (0=newest, 1=second newest, ...).
tools.name: link_peek

id.description: Target session — accepts session id or name (as shown in WebUI tab).

scope.description: Detail level. status=~50tok, brief=~200tok, last=~500-2000tok (default), recent=~500-1500tok, full=~2000-8000tok.

turn.description: Turn index from newest (0=latest turn, 1=previous, ...). Only used with scope "last" or "full".

tools.description: Send a message to another session. If idle: starts a new flow (like user typing). If running: injects via synthetic tool call (cache-friendly, no prefix rebuild). Use abort=true to stop the target first. Use mode="alert" for FYI messages.
tools.name: link_post

abort.description: If true, abort the target session first, then send message.

attachments.description: Optional local files/images to upload into a Hub chatroom. Each item must include a local path. Supported for __hub__:room targets.

broadcast.description: If true, send to all channel members.

id.description: Target session id or name, or channel_id.

mode.description: Message type. "reply" (default) for feedback/instructions, "alert" for FYI.

tools.description: Block until a target session stops (run_complete/error) or timeout. Returns trigger reason and whether the run was started by a user or by a link_post. Use timeout to periodically peek at progress instead of blocking forever.
tools.name: link_wait

async.description: If true, do not block — register an async trigger and return immediately. When the target event fires, this session will be woken up with a message. Note: on="idle" triggers on ANY terminal state (including error and interrupted), not just successful completion. Default: false (synchronous blocking).

channel.description: Channel ID to watch (alternative to session).

on.description: Event type to wait for. Default: "idle".

session.description: Session id or name to watch.

filter.description: Optional content filter. Only meaningful for chatroom sessions with on="message". For non-chatroom sessions, filter is ignored. Supports glob patterns.

persistent.description: If true, trigger repeatedly (stays active after each fire). If false (default), auto-cancel after first trigger.

timeout.description: Timeout in ms. Default: 300000 (5min). Use -1 for infinite.

tools.description: List all available personas with their name, display name, description, and whether they are currently active. Personas are complete working modes that combine tool permissions and skills.
tools.name: list_personas

tools.description:
Browse the Lux help wiki and changelog. Use to explain Lux features to the user or introspect version changes.

Topics:
- "index" — list all available help sections
- "wiki:<id>" — read a specific help section (e.g. "wiki:getting-started", "wiki:tools")
- "changelog" — recent version changes (paginated, skips version bump CI commits)

Returns paginated text content. Use the `page` parameter to navigate.
tools.name: lux_help

page.description: Page number (1-based). Default: 1. Each page is ~80 lines for wiki, ~40 entries for changelog.

topic.description: What to read. "index" for help TOC, "wiki:<section_id>" for a specific doc, "changelog" for version history.

tools.description: Add a memo/reminder to the personal备忘录. Use this when the user asks you to remember something, set a reminder, or record a quick note they don't want to forget. Examples: "每天下班前检查xxx进度", "周五前确认电源方案", "xx月xx日是客户A的死期".
tools.name: memo_add

content.description: Memo content. Keep it concise and actionable.

remind_at.description: Optional reminder time in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM). E.g. "2026-05-07 18:00" for a specific time, or just "2026-05-07" for that day.

repeat_rule.description: Optional repeat rule. Only meaningful when remind_at is set.

tools.description: Mark a memo as done or undone. Use when the user says they've completed something or wants to reactivate a completed memo.
tools.name: memo_done

done.description: true = mark done, false = mark undone (reactivate). Default: true.

tools.description: List personal memos. Use to check what reminders and notes are pending. Filter by status, tags, or search keywords.
tools.name: memo_list

filter.description: Filter by status. "active" = not done (default), "done" = completed, "all" = everything.

tools.description: Consult the project oracle — a session snapshot with deep project knowledge. Requires LUX.oracle in the current working directory and fails immediately when the snapshot is missing. Use when you need architectural context, design intent, or cross-cutting knowledge without exploring the codebase yourself.
tools.name: oracle_query

question.description: Natural language question about the project.

tools.description: Abort the running singleton playbook by playbookId and abort active playbook child sessions. Fails if the playbook is not running or was already aborted.
tools.name: playbook_abort

tools.description: Archive a playbook by moving LUX_HOME/playbooks/<id> to LUX_HOME/playbooks_archived/<id>. Preserves project files, run history, logs, and artifacts. Hidden from default list. Refuses while the singleton run is active.
tools.name: playbook_archive

tools.description: Create a Lux playbook npm project under LUX_HOME/playbooks/<id>. The generated playbook.mjs is the canonical script; agents should edit files in that project directly after creation.
tools.name: playbook_create

script.description: Optional native Node.js ESM playbook.mjs content. If omitted, Lux creates a minimal starter. Scripts run with local system access, global lux/agent/parallel/pipeline, per-playbook node_modules, and finish flat scripts via lux.done(result).

tools.description: Delete a playbook npm project. Destructive: permanently removes project files, run history, logs, and artifacts. Use only when the user explicitly asks. Refuses while the singleton run is active.
tools.name: playbook_delete

tools.description: Execute the playbook singleton by playbookId. Lux reads the current playbook.mjs from the playbook project at execution time. Fails if the playbook is already running; use playbook_status to inspect childSessionIds or playbook_abort to stop it first.
tools.name: playbook_execute

tools.description: List playbook npm projects. By default returns active playbooks only; pass includeArchived or archivedOnly to inspect playbooks moved under LUX_HOME/playbooks_archived/<id>.
tools.name: playbook_list

includeArchived.description: Include archived playbooks in the result.

tools.description: Get the singleton playbook status by playbookId, including result/error, log tail, artifacts, and child session ids for direct peek/intervention.
tools.name: playbook_status

tools.description: Restore an archived playbook by moving LUX_HOME/playbooks_archived/<id> back to LUX_HOME/playbooks/<id>.
tools.name: playbook_unarchive

tools.description: List active event subscriptions for this session.
tools.name: poll_list

tools.description:
Subscribe to external events. When a matching event arrives, this session will be woken up (if idle) or receive an injection (if running).

Source patterns: "wechat:message", "wechat:*", "webhook:*", "*"
Tag filters: optional key-value pairs for fine-grained filtering (AND match).

Mode:
- "wake" (default): auto-wakes idle sessions, injects when running

Note: "inject" and "queue" modes are reserved but not implemented yet. Use debounceMs to batch rapid-fire events (e.g. 5000 for 5s window).
tools.name: poll_subscribe

debounceMs.description: Debounce window in ms. Events within window are batched. Default: 0 (no debounce). E.g. 5000 for 5s.

mode.description: Delivery mode. Only "wake" is currently supported. Default: "wake".

persistent.description: If false, auto-unsubscribe after first event. Default: true.

tagFilters.description: Optional tag filters (AND match). Supports glob wildcards: "*开发*" for contains, "俊朗*" for prefix. E.g. {"session_name":"*开发*"}, {"sender_name":"俊朗"}, {"is_group":"true"}.

tools.description: Unsubscribe from external events. Provide a subscription id to remove a specific one, or omit to unsubscribe all for this session.
tools.name: poll_unsubscribe

id.description: Subscription id (e.g. "p_a1b2c3") or source pattern (e.g. "wechat:message") to remove. Omit to remove all subscriptions for this session.

tools.description: I examine the contents of a file. Returns numbered lines for precise reference. Supports text, images, and PDFs. Path must be absolute. Before changing any file, this is always my first step. To find files by name, I use glob. To search content across files, I use grep.
tools.name: read

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to read. Supports text files, image files (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp), and PDF files (.pdf).

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read. Defaults to all lines.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files.

tools.description: Load an entire git project into context as structured Markdown. Levels: summary (overview) → tree (file list) → headers (first ~30 lines) → signatures (LSP symbols, optional) → full (complete, budgeted) → all (everything, 1M+ models only). Uses git ls-files for tracked files only.
tools.name: read_repo

exclude.description: Glob — skip matching files. Uses the same semantics as the glob tool; basename-only patterns like "*.test.ts" match recursively.

include.description: Glob — only matching files. Uses the same semantics as the glob tool; basename-only patterns like "*.ts" match recursively.

level.description: summary (~2-5K tok), tree (~5-20K), headers (~30-100K), signatures (~50-200K, needs LSP), full (~200-600K), all (1M+ only).

tools.description: Read text aloud to the user via Text-to-Speech. Use for important notifications, task completions, key findings, or conversational replies — speak naturally and concisely, as if talking to the user face to face. Do NOT use for code output, raw data, JSON, or verbose technical content. The text is sent to the user's browser where it is synthesised into speech. Keep each call under ~500 characters for best latency; for longer content, call multiple times.
tools.name: read_tts

text.description: The text to speak aloud. Should be natural language, not code or markup.

tools.description: Search memories by keyword, tag, or kind. Returns id + hint list. Use empty query to list all memories.
tools.name: recall

query.description: Search keyword (searches name, summary, content, tags, props)

tools.description: Save a memory entry (fact or episode) for cross-session recall. Creates an unanchored note — consolidation agent will later extract entities and relationships.
tools.name: remember

tools.description: Create a Lux routine npm project under LUX_HOME/routines/<id> with package.json lux.routine metadata and routine.mjs. Routines require inputSchema/outputSchema and must call lux.done(result).
tools.name: routine_create

script.description: Optional native Node.js ESM routine.mjs content. If omitted, Lux creates a minimal starter.

tools.description: Delete a Lux routine npm project under LUX_HOME/routines/<id>. Refuses while the routine has a running run.
tools.name: routine_delete

tools.description: Get routine invocation metadata: id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, timeoutMs. Does not return source code or run history.
tools.name: routine_get

tools.description: Run a finite Lux routine by id with structured input. Validates input/output schemas, waits for lux.done(result), returns result directly, and fails as a tool error on routine failure.
tools.name: routine_run

tools.description: Search Lux routines by id/description. Returns id and description only.
tools.name: routine_search

tools.description: Save the current configuration (base persona + overlaid skills/tools) as a new user persona. The saved persona can be recalled later with switch_persona.
tools.name: save_persona

description.description: Description of what this persona does.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name (e.g. "Rust 开发者", "网络探索者").

name.description: Internal name for the new persona (e.g. "rust-dev", "net-explorer").

tools.description: I execute a script and return the output. Use this for programmatic tasks — data transformation, JSON manipulation, complex string processing, math computation, regex extraction, date calculation, or any logic that benefits from a real programming language. By default runs Node.js ES module (top-level await supported). Use `import` syntax, NOT `require()`. Use console.log() to produce output. This is preferred over `bash node -e` for multi-line logic.
tools.name: script

code.description: The script code to execute. Default runtime is Node.js ESM — use `import` syntax (not `require`). Use console.log()/print() for output.

cwd.description: Working directory for the script process. Relative paths resolve against the current session cwd. Defaults to the current session cwd.

lang.description: Script runtime. Default: "node" (ES module). Options: "node" (ESM, lux.xxx() bridge available), "node-cjs" (CommonJS, require() ok, bridge available), "python" (Python 3). Or any installed interpreter name.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds).

tools.description: Create a new Lux session. Returns the session id. The session starts idle and can receive messages via link_post. Use type="chatroom" to create a shared message board with no agent — other sessions can post/peek/wait on it for multi-agent collaboration.
tools.name: session_create

persona.description: Optional persona name for the new session (e.g. "developer", "reviewer"). If omitted, the new session uses the default persona. Ignored for chatroom type.

type.description: Session type. "agent" (default) creates a normal agent session. "chatroom" creates a shared message board with no agent — multiple sessions can post messages and read history.

tools.description: Destroy (close) an existing Lux session by name or id. The session process is terminated and removed.
tools.name: session_destroy

id.description: Session id or name to destroy.

tools.description: Spawn a subagent that runs independently in the background. Provide a short description (3-5 words) that will be slugified into a task_id internally. The parent flow continues immediately without waiting. Use subagent_wait or subagent_output with the task_id to check results later.
tools.name: subagent

description.description: A short 3-5 word description of the task (e.g. "analyze server logs"). Will be slugified to create a unique task_id.

inherit_canvas.description: If true, the subagent inherits the parent's full canvas context instead of starting blank. A synthetic fork notice is injected so the subagent knows it was forked and should only complete the given task. Default: false.

persona.description: Optional persona name for the subagent (e.g. "reviewer", "explorer"). Sets tool permissions + skills automatically. If omitted, inherits the parent agent's persona.

prompt.description: The task prompt / instructions for the subagent.

tools.description: List all subagents with their current status.
tools.name: subagent_list

tools.description: Check the status and output of a subagent. By default, returns immediately without blocking. Set block=true to wait for output (with optional timeout). Returns status (running/completed/failed/aborted) and result if available.
tools.name: subagent_output

block.description: If true, block and wait for the subagent to produce output. Default: false.

task_id.description: The task_id of the subagent to check.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds when blocking. Only used when block=true.

tools.description: Inspect a subagent without blocking. Returns status plus recent visible events/output. Use scope to control detail level and page to paginate older event history.
tools.name: subagent_peek

page.description: Event page index from newest (0=newest, 1=previous, ...). Default: 0.

scope.description: Detail level. status=metadata only, brief=short output, last=latest page (default), recent=more events, full=largest page.

task_id.description: The task_id of the subagent to inspect.

tools.description: Send a sideband message to a running subagent. The subagent receives it as a synthetic sideband tool result at its next interrupt checkpoint, allowing the parent to guide or correct it without aborting.
tools.name: subagent_post

message.description: Message/instructions to inject into the subagent.

task_id.description: The task_id of the target subagent.

tools.description: Stop a running subagent. If the subagent has already completed, this is a no-op.
tools.name: subagent_stop

task_id.description: The task_id of the subagent to stop.

tools.description: Wait for a subagent to complete and return its result. Use the task_id assigned when the subagent was spawned. If the task is already done, returns immediately. If still running, blocks until completion.
tools.name: subagent_wait

task_id.description: The task_id of the subagent to wait for.

tools.description: Switch to a named persona. A persona is a complete working mode combining tool permissions and skills. This replaces the active tool permissions and skills. Use list_personas first to see available personas.
tools.name: switch_persona

name.description: The name of the persona to switch to (e.g. "developer", "reviewer", "architect").

tools.description: I create a new task item to track work. The task list is pinned in the canvas and auto-removed when all items are completed.
tools.name: task_create

active_form.description: Optional short text describing the current active form or step of the task (shown in TUI).

blocked_by.description: Optional array of task IDs (names) that must complete before this task can start.

id.description: A short unique name for this task (e.g. "setup_db", "fix_auth"). Used to reference the task later. Must be unique.

metadata.description: Optional metadata object to attach to the task.

subject.description: Brief human-readable subject for the task.

tools.description: I delete a task by ID, or clear all tasks. Cleans up dependency references.
tools.name: task_delete

all.description: If true, clear the entire task list.

task_id.description: The ID of the task to delete.

tools.description: I get full details of a single task by ID, including dependencies, owner, and metadata.
tools.name: task_get

task_id.description: The ID of the task to retrieve.

tools.description: I list all task items with status. Shows blocked [B] and owner [O:name] indicators. Use to review tasks and find IDs.
tools.name: task_list

tools.description: I update a task item. When all items are completed the task list pin is auto-removed. Use task_list to find IDs. Set status to "deleted" to remove a task.
tools.name: task_update

active_form.description: Optional short text describing the current active form or step of the task (shown in TUI).

add_blocked_by.description: Array of task IDs to add as blockers for this task.

add_blocks.description: Array of task IDs that this task should block (adds this task to their blockedBy).

metadata.description: Metadata to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

owner.description: Set the owner of this task (e.g. a subagent taskName).

task_id.description: The unique name of the task to update.

tools.description: Attach a remote Lux Worker and route host-bound tools (read/glob/grep/bash/write/edit/script/read_repo) to it with fail-closed semantics. Supports uri=ssh://user:password-or-passphrase@host[:port]?cwd=/path&pem=/path/key, or access_code + relay_url for relay workers. Use only credentials explicitly provided by the user.
tools.name: worker_attach

access_code.description: Relay access code for an already-running lux-worker relay session.

relay_url.description: Operator relay URL. Optional when worker.relayUrl or LUX_WORKER_OPERATOR_URL/LUX_WORKER_RELAY_URL is configured.

uri.description: Worker URI. Currently supports ssh://user:password-or-passphrase@host[:port]. If cwd is omitted for SSH, the remote account home is used.

tools.description: Detach the current Lux Worker, close its transport, unregister worker operator tools, and return host-bound tools to the local machine. Also broadcasts worker_status so WebUI reflects the change.
tools.name: worker_detach

tools.description: I create or overwrite a file. Creates parent directories automatically. For modifying existing files, I prefer edit — write is for genuinely new files or complete rewrites. IMPORTANT: When writing content longer than ~300 lines, I MUST split the work — first write the initial portion, then use one or more edit calls to append or fill in remaining sections. Writing very long content in a single call risks provider output truncation and silent data loss.
tools.name: write

content.description: The content to write to the file.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to write.
